findings.title: Full success-criterion coverage with no scope creep
findings.description: Every functional criterion is traced: purity/no state write/no `sq` spawn to 5.1 (and 6.3 walkthrough), Phase 0 concept prompt to 5.1 and 6.3, byte identity to 2.1–2.2 and 6.1, CLI/MCP parity to 5.1, and the guide warning to 3.5, 3.6 and the explicit 6.1 guard. Technical criteria map to 3.3/6.2 (`services/` imports), 6.2 (export audit), and 3.2a/3.7/6.1 (lint, typecheck, tests). Code deletions (D1–D4) map to sections 3 and 4, and the 269 integration requirement is satisfied by the removals themselves. No task introduces behavior the design excludes; the "kept" and "excluded" lists in Context Summary are respected.

findings.title: Sequencing, commit points, and test-with patterns are sound
findings.description: The golden capture is explicitly gated before any source edit, which D6 requires. The cross-package dist/typecheck ordering between 3.4 and 3.5/3.6 is called out, and 3.3–3.6 are intentionally one commit because they cannot compile apart. Commits are plain lines at verified points (2.3, 3.2a, 3.7, 4.1–4.4, 5.1, conditional 6.3) — not after every task and not only at the end. Test edits sit inside their implementation tasks (3.1/3.2, 3.3, 3.5, 3.6, 4.1–4.4) with a full suite at 3.7 and 6.1, so the test-with pattern holds. No circular dependencies; the conditional 6.3 commit handles late fixes without leaving an untested commit.

findings.title: Golden-capture success check is self-contradictory as written
findings.description: Task 2.2 says to "Remove the write step before committing" and then "Run the test twice. **Success:** both runs pass, and `git status` shows the golden files unchanged after the second run." Once the write step is removed, the test only compares against goldens; it can no longer capture or rewrite them, so "the golden files unchanged after the second run" is a static condition rather than evidence of determinism, and the text does not tell the executor at which point to remove the write step relative to the two runs. A junior could either capture, remove the step, then run twice (the intended reading), or try to run twice with the write step still present and destroy the just-captured goldens. Reorder the steps explicitly: capture once with the write step → remove the write step → run twice and check `git status`. The same pattern appears in 5.1 ("confirm the snapshot assertion fails, then revert"), where the expected-failure outcome should also be a named success condition rather than an unstated one.

findings.title: Proportionality and convention adherence
findings.description: Six top-level tasks with focused atomic subtasks fit an effort-2/5 slice: each task maps to a named design decision (D1–D6) or migration-plan row, and the four golden/parity/purity/walkthrough tests map one-to-one to distinct success criteria — no surplus test tasks. Steps stay behavioral ("delete section 3.4", "assert both are unchanged") rather than dictating implementation the slice does not require, and conventions from AGENTS.md are observed: no merge/push task, no PM confirmation gate, constants-at-top rule for new test assertions, and the explicit `unverified`-style warning that the compiler will not catch orphan exports (4.2/6.2 grep checks). No load/NFR task is needed — the slice design restates no NFR.
